DEVELOPER INSIGHTS

A Risk Register for Ground Engineering That Drives Action

Use the register to assign decisions and evidence, not to collect generic concerns.

In this insight

Describe the uncertainty concretelyAssign ownership that matches authoritySeparate mitigation from optimismReview at meaningful transitionsFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Describe the uncertainty concretely

A useful risk entry states what is uncertain, how it could affect the project and what evidence or action is needed. Avoid entries such as ground risk without further explanation. Link the issue to a location, activity or assumption where possible. The register should help the team understand the decision in front of it, rather than simply demonstrate that risks have been listed.

Assign ownership that matches authority

The person managing an action may not be able to resolve the underlying design or third-party issue. Identify both the action owner and the decision authority. Give the action a date linked to the programme. This prevents the register from becoming a collection of overdue items assigned to people who cannot obtain the required outcome.

Separate mitigation from optimism

A statement that the contractor will manage the issue is not a defined response. Record the proposed investigation, review, coordination or contingency process and the evidence of completion. The technical team must determine the appropriate engineering response. The project controls team should track whether the agreed action has actually occurred and whether the remaining uncertainty has changed.

Review at meaningful transitions

Update the register when new information arrives, the design changes or the project moves into a new stage. Close items with a reason and retain relevant evidence. Keep residual obligations visible to the next team. A concise, current register can guide commercial allowances and programme priorities more effectively than a large generic list that remains unchanged from tender to handover.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Describe specific uncertainty and consequence.
  • Assign actions to people with a route to decision.
  • Review the register when project conditions change.
